title: Platform runbook, roadmap, and retrospectives - systems & services
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the Platform team’s systems and services runbook, current roadmap highlights (Q4 2025 → H1 2026), standardized how-tos for common platform tasks, dashboard & alert guidance, and a short retrospective summary of major incidents and follow-ups. It is intended to be the single operational reference for engineers oncall for platform systems (control plane, observability, autoscaling, and shared infra services).

Owner & Scope

- Owner: Platform Engineering (eng-platform)
- Oncall: Platform SRE rotation (see team wiki for weekly roster)
- Scope: platform control plane services (k8s control, routing, config, auth), shared services (logging, metrics, tracing, alert pipeline), autoscaling, capacity management, and console APIs that surface platform health.

Table of contents

1) Runbook: top-level incident playbooks
2) Dashboards & Alerts: SLOs, thresholds, example rules
3) How-tos: standard operational procedures
4) Roadmap: priorities & milestones
5) Retrospective highlights & action tracker
6) Ownership, escalation, and links

1) Runbook: top-level incident playbooks

1.1 Incident classification

- Priority P0: Platform-wide outage impacting all customer API requests or console access for >5 minutes or >20% of customers.
- Priority P1: Significant degradation (high error rate, sustained latency increases) affecting a subset of customers or routes.
- Priority P2: Non-critical failures with impact to non-customer-facing ops (e.g., internal metrics delay).

1.2 Initial responder checklist (first 10 minutes)

1. Acknowledge incident in PagerDuty; add short summary to incident Slack channel (#inc-plat).
2. Capture scope: which services, regions, models, and customer tiers are impacted.
3. Post initial status: Incident declared (P0/P1) and remediation owner assigned.
4. If customer-facing, trigger status page update and notify CS/Support.

1.3 Triage steps (10–30 minutes)

- Check primary dashboards: control-plane-ops, api-latency, autoscaler-health, ingress-errors.
- Run quick sanity commands: kubectl get pods -n platform, check leader election, check etcd cluster health.
- If error budget burn is high, enable temporary rate-limiting fallback policy.

1.4 Mitigation actions (30–120 minutes)

- Apply quick rollback to previous deployment artifact if recent change is suspected.
- Isolate problematic nodes (cordon + drain) and scale up known-good node pool.
- Apply circuit breaker: route traffic to backup region or dedicated capacity pool.
- For datastore issues: enable read-only fallback and surface degraded mode.

1.5 Post-incident steps

- Run the incident postmortem template within 72 hours and assign owners for action items.
- Implement hotfixes and validate under load.
- Track long-lived items in the Platform team backlog and surface to PLM for roadmap prioritization.

2) Dashboards & Alerts: SLOs, thresholds, example rules

2.1 Key SLOs (owned by platform)

- Control plane API availability: 99.95% monthly (success rate for control-plane endpoints).
- Serving API p99 latency: <250ms target (hosted API within region).
- Metrics pipeline freshness: 95% of metrics within 60s latency.

2.2 Alerting principles

- Prefer actionable alerts (requires human) vs informational.
- Pair alerts with runbook links and runbook severity in the alert message.
- Use composite alerts to reduce noise (e.g., only alert on sustained p95/p99 deviations for >5 minutes).

2.3 Example Prometheus rules (YAML snippet)

- Control plane API error rate (alert after 5m sustained > 3%):

groups:
- name: control-plane.rules
  rules:
  - alert: ControlPlaneHighErrorRate
    expr: sum(rate(control_plane_http_requests_total{code!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(control_plane_http_requests_total[5m])) > 0.03
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: major
    annotations:
      summary: "Control plane error rate > 3% ({{ $value }})"
      runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/platform-runbook-roadmap-2026#Runbook"

- Metrics pipeline freshness (alert after 3m missing):

  - alert: MetricsPipelineStale
    expr: max(time() - last_over_time(metrics_ingest_timestamp[10m])) > 180
    for: 3m
    labels:
      severity: minor
    annotations:
      summary: "Metrics ingestion pipeline stale > 3m"
      runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/platform-runbook-roadmap-2026#Runbook"

2.4 Dashboards to monitor

- Platform Overview (service map, top errors, region health)
- Control Plane (API latency, error rate, leader elections, etcd health)
- Autoscaler Health (scale events, queue length, batch latency)
- Observability Pipeline (ingest rate, backfill lag, retention warnings)
- Capacity & Cost (GPU pool utilization, reserved capacity headroom)

3) How-tos: standard operational procedures

3.1 Onboard a new platform service (4-step checklist)

1. Create service repo with platform-service-template and register in service-catalog.
2. Add k8s manifests with resource requests/limits, liveness/readiness probes, and a basic Prometheus scrape config.
3. Add SLO and error budget definition to the service README and add basic dashboards (Grafana) using the shared grafana-template.
4. Add alert rules to platform-alerts repo and run the chaos test in staging (5 minutes of degraded network).

3.2 Deploy rollback procedure (safe rollback)

- Confirm previous image digest (avoid latest tags).
- kubectl set image deployment/<svc> <container>=<image>@sha256:<digest> -n <ns>
- Monitor deployment rollout status: kubectl rollout status deployment/<svc> -n <ns>
- If rollback target fails, scale down new revision and scale up last-known-good revision.

3.3 Add a Grafana panel and link to runbook

- Use grafana-cli or the dashboard JSON template. Ensure panels include a link to the runbook (annotation) and an ownership tag: owner:team/eng-platform.

3.4 Access & credentials rotation

- Use vault.redwood.io for service credentials; follow the secrets rotation playbook in /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth. Rotate keys every 90 days or immediately after exposure.

4) Roadmap: priorities & milestones (Q4 2025 → H1 2026)

4.1 Near-term priorities (next 3 months)

- Observability hardening: reduce alert noise by 40% (investigate top 10 noisy alerts).
- Safe autoscaling improvements: introduce cooldown windows and request-aware scaling policies.
- Runbook coverage: ensure 100% critical path coverage for P0/P1 incidents.

4.2 Mid-term (3–6 months)

- Multi-region automatic failover for control plane.
- Platform cost controls: dynamic routing to cheaper model variants under non-critical SLOs.
- Developer experience: self-service service registration and dashboard provisioning.

4.3 Roadmap milestones with owners

- M1 (2026-03): Alert noise reduction complete — owner: Observability Squad (Ben Harper).
- M2 (2026-04): Autoscaler v2 rollout in staging — owner: Runtime & Autoscale (Priya Desai).
- M3 (2026-06): Multi-region control plane pilot — owner: Platform Systems (Aisha Patel).

5) Retrospective highlights & action tracker

5.1 Recent incidents (summary)

- Incident: Metrics pipeline outage, 2025-11-02 — root cause: consumer lag from a schema change; impact: dashboard gaps for 2.5 hours. Action: add contract tests and schema validation to ingest pipeline. Owner: Observability Squad.
- Incident: Autoscaler thrash, 2025-12-18 — root cause: aggressive scale-down policy + noisy health checks; impact: transient request failures for some customers. Action: implement cooldown window and improve health checks. Owner: Runtime & Autoscale.

5.2 Action tracker (open items)

- Add synthetic transactions for control plane endpoints — due 2026-01-15 — owner: Platform Systems — status: complete.
- Add chaos test to pre-prod for autoscaler changes — due 2026-03-01 — owner: Runtime & Autoscale — status: in_progress.
- Implement alert suppression during regular maintenance windows — due 2026-02-28 — owner: Observability — status: in_progress.

6) Ownership, escalation, and links

- Primary contacts:
  - Platform Systems: Aisha Patel (owner) — aisha@redwood.ai
  - Observability Squad: Ben Harper — ben@redwood.ai
  - Runtime & Autoscale: Priya Desai — priya@redwood.ai

- Escalation matrix:
  1. Oncall engineer (PagerDuty primary)
  2. Squad lead (if unresolved >30m)
  3. Platform CTO oncall (if unresolved >2h or P0)

- Useful links:
  - Service catalog: /confluence/eng-platform/service-catalog
  - Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/dashboards
  - PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/teams/redwood-platform
  - Incident template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

Appendix: quick commands

- Check leader election and pods: kubectl get pods -n platform -o wide
- Check etcd health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl endpoint status --write-out=table --endpoints=<etcd endpoints>
- Restart a single problematic service: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<svc> -n <ns>

Revision history

If you are oncall and unsure of the next step, @mention the oncall lead in #inc-plat and follow the initial responder checklist above.
